column2: Love and keeping the Lord's charge, ordinances and judgments continue throughout life; the three obligation terms remain.
The contrast concerns the present hearers and their children, who did not experience the discipline and mighty acts. I speak unto you makes the elliptical contrast intelligible.
column3: The supplied speaking clause is explanatory English grammar rather than an expressed Greek clause; the long construction continues through 11:7.

column2: Signs and wonders concern Pharaoh and all his land in Egypt, extending the remembered experience.
Egypt's force, chariots and mounted contingent are overwhelmed in the Red Sea while pursuing Israel, with destruction lasting to today.
column3: The selected collective hippos is inherited as horsemen; horses or cavalry may better preserve its precise range and needs further lexical review.

column2: The Lord's wilderness actions continue until arrival at the present place, keeping the experiential sequence.
Dathan and Abiram are identified through Eliab and Reuben; earth swallows them, houses, tents and their substance before all Israel.
column3: Substance for hypostasis here concerns what belonged with them; the exact scope of possessions or household establishment needs fuller contextual review.

column2: Your eyes have seen all the great works concludes the contrast with the children; today remains in the selected wording.
All commands are to be kept for life, multiplication and entry into the Jordan-crossing inheritance; the repeated inheritance language remains.
Long days belong in the land sworn to fathers and descendants, described as flowing with milk and honey.
Egyptian sowing and watering with feet are compared to a herb garden; the selected agricultural image remains without inventing a mechanism.
The new land's hills and plains drink heaven's rain, preserving the personified land image.
The Lord cares for the land with eyes continually upon it from the year's beginning to end; the full temporal span remains.
Diligent hearing of all commandments involves love and service from all heart and soul; both inward terms remain.
He gives timely early and latter rain, enabling grain, wine and oil harvest; selected third-person He is retained.
Propose livestock for cattle because the selected generic animal term covers the field-fed domestic animals broadly. Eating and fullness still lead into the warning.
The selected enlarged-heart wording precedes transgression, other-god service and worship; it is not silently replaced with deceived.
column3: The moral force of the enlarged-heart image needs further lexical and contextual review; retention does not resolve the metaphor.

column2: Wrath shuts heaven, removes rain and fruit, and brings rapid loss of the good land; each consequence remains.
Words belong in heart and soul and as a hand sign immovable before the eyes; the selected repeated formulation remains.

Propose making the children the speakers and subjects of sitting, walking, lying and rising. The accusative participles follow the children and infinitive speak, unlike the nominative parent-directed construction in 6:7. Teach your children to speak of them naturally represents the repeated word-object through one English complement.
Doorposts of houses and gates receive the words in writing, retaining both locations.
The days of Israel and its sons are prolonged like heaven's days upon earth, preserving the source's expansive comparison.
Diligent hearing includes love for the Lord our God, walking all His ways and cleaving to Him; selected our remains.
The Lord casts out all these nations and Israel inherits greater, stronger nations; both agents remain distinct.
The footprint promise spans wilderness, Anti-Lebanon, Euphrates and western sea; the selected mountain range remains.
No opponent can stand, and dread and fear extend across every trodden land, preserving both fear terms.
A blessing and a curse are set before Israel today, introducing the paired conditions.
The blessing depends on hearing today's commanded words of the Lord.
The selected plural curses follows disobedience and departure to unknown gods, retaining both number and full condition.
Blessing belongs on Gerizim and curse on Ebal after entry; the two mountains are not reversed.
The rhetorical location question retains westward Canaan, Gilgal and the lofty oak rather than substituting Moreh.
column3: The compressed geographic construction remains provisional; no modern map identification or apparatus choice is claimed.

column2: Jordan crossing leads to perpetual possession, inheritance and dwelling; the source's repeated land-acquisition wording remains.
All ordinances and these judgments set before Israel today must be performed, closing the charge.
The ordinances and judgments govern all the days of life in the land given by the fathers' God.
Every former worship place on high mountains, hills and under the leafy tree is to be destroyed; all locations remain.
Altars, pillars, sacred groves and carved divine images receive distinct destruction actions, ending with loss of their name from the place.
The prohibition of doing so to the Lord introduces the contrasting chosen-place instruction.
The Lord chooses one tribal location for His name to be named and invoked, and Israel seeks and enters it.
Burnt offerings, sacrifices, firstfruits, vows, freewill gifts and firstborn cattle and sheep all remain; no tithe item is imported into this selected list.
Households eat and rejoice before the Lord in all their undertakings because of His blessing.
Present practice of each doing what pleases himself is prohibited for the future, retaining the comparison with today.
The reason is that rest and inheritance have not yet been reached; both promised conditions remain.
Crossing, dwelling, rest from surrounding enemies and secure residence form the promised sequence.
The chosen place receives burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, firstfruits, gifts and choice vowed gifts; the fuller list remains distinct from 12:6.
Sons, daughters, male and female slaves and the Levite rejoice, with the Levite's lack of share and inheritance explaining inclusion.
Whole burnt offerings may not be offered at every place seen, retaining the broad prohibition.
Only the chosen tribal location receives them, and all today's commands are to be done there; there is repeated.
Ordinary slaughter and eating according to desire is permitted in every city, with clean and unclean together as for gazelle or deer.
Blood is the exception and must be poured on earth like water; both prohibition and comparison remain.
Tithes of grain, wine and oil, firstborn cattle and sheep, vows, pledged offerings and hand-firstfruits may not be eaten in the towns.
column3: The distinction between pledged offerings and the neighbouring vow and freewill categories needs specialist ritual-terminology review.

column2: Eating occurs before the Lord at His chosen place with son, daughter, both slave groups and the sojourner; selected sojourner is not replaced by Levite.
The Levite must not be forsaken throughout life in the land; the negative and full duration remain explicit.
Expanded borders and desire for meat lead to permission to eat according to the soul's desire, preserving the repeated flesh and desire terms.
Distance from the chosen place permits local slaughter of cattle and sheep and eating by desire; the specifically bovine cattle remains.
Gazelle and deer illustrate ordinary consumption by clean and unclean alike, retaining the paired animals and persons.
Strong care against blood-eating is grounded in blood as life; the life is not to be eaten with flesh.
The prohibition and pouring on earth like water are repeated in full.
Not eating blood serves welfare of the hearer and sons when doing good and pleasing before the Lord.
Holy things and vowed offerings still go to the chosen place where His name is invoked, preserving the exception to local consumption.
Burnt-offering flesh goes on the altar; sacrificial blood is poured at its base and flesh eaten. The selected base detail remains.
column3: The transition between burnt offerings and other sacrifices requires careful ritual reading; the text is not expanded to prescribe eating burnt offerings.

column2: Keep, hear and do all words remain three responses linked to lasting welfare and good, pleasing conduct.
Destruction of the former nations, inheritance and settlement introduce the warning against adopting their practice.
Seeking their gods or imitating their service after their destruction is prohibited; the imagined inquiry and resolve remain quoted.
The hated abominations include burning both sons and daughters to their gods, retaining the explicit reason for refusing imitation.
The no-addition/no-subtraction command remains at this chapter opening under the selected numbering, following chapter twelve's thirty-one units.
A prophet or dreamer gives a sign or wonder, initiating a conditional case rather than an assertion of authority.
Even fulfillment of the sign accompanies the invitation to serve unknown gods; the successful sign is not omitted.
The prophet or dreamer must not be heard because the Lord tests whole-heart and whole-soul love; both alternatives and both inner terms remain.
Following, fear, command-keeping, hearing and being joined to the Lord remain; no absent service clause is imported from another form.
Death is prescribed for leading away from the redeemer and commanded way, followed by removal of the evil person from the community.
The secret enticer may be a paternal or maternal brother, son, daughter, intimate wife or soul-equal friend; the selected paternal alternative remains.
The other gods may belong to near or far nations across earth's entire extent, retaining both alternatives.
Consent, hearing, pity, yearning and concealment are all denied; selected yearning is retained rather than automatically changed to sparing.
Surely report him preserves the selected emphatic reporting command, followed by the hearer's hands first and all people's hands afterward.
The plural executioners stone him because he sought separation from the deliverer from Egypt and bondage; the violent action and reason remain.
All Israel hears and fears and ceases such evil, preserving the stated deterrent result.
A report in one of the given cities introduces the communal case.
Lawless men from among Israel turn all inhabitants toward unknown gods; all and the internal origin remain.
Inquiry and diligent search must establish the matter clearly true before the ensuing action; the evidential condition remains.
All inhabitants are killed by sword and the city with all in it devoted to destruction; no unexpressed separate livestock clause is added.
All spoil is gathered in streets and burned with the city before the Lord, leaving permanent uninhabitedness and no rebuilding.
column3: All together renders pandemei provisionally; whether it particularly specifies participation of the whole people merits further review.

column2: Nothing devoted may remain in the hand; turning wrath, granting mercy, showing mercy and multiplying remain distinct promised responses.
Hearing, keeping all today's commandments and doing good and pleasing before the Lord complete the conditional promise.
